html:
SMTO-SKL-0032 — SMTO couldn't find you on this invitation's guest list

GUID: 19394c57-882b-5c08-b4a4-baa8142ab9c6
Slug: google-calendar-self-attendee-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • SMTO tried to accept or decline this invitation for you, but the Google account it used isn't listed as a guest on it. Your reply was not sent and nothing on the event changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the event in Google Calendar and look at its guest list. Note which of your email addresses was invited. SMTO can only reply for an address that appears on the guest list.
  2. Ask SMTO which Google accounts it has connected. If the invited address is a different account, tell SMTO to use that account for the reply. Replying through the wrong account fails because that account isn't a guest.
  3. If the invitation went to a group or mailing-list address instead of you, or the event has no guest list, reply directly in Google Calendar instead. In those cases Google doesn't mark you as a guest on the event, so SMTO has no reply of yours to change.

What success looks like

  • The event in Google Calendar shows your reply (Yes, No or Maybe) next to your name.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to change another guest's reply to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Calendar respond operation found no single attendee marked self with an email address on the event, so no RSVP was sent.

What this means

  • Responding to an invitation cannot find exactly one attendee marked self with an email address. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Responding to an invitation cannot find exactly one attendee marked self with an email address.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected attendee account and self markers in the current event.

How to fix it

  • CalendarService._write (respond) requires exactly one attendee with self=true and an email on the pre-read event. Read the event under the intended google_account (google_calendar.event with the exact account_ref) and respond only when Google marks exactly one attendee as self; never edit another attendee's response.
  • Read the invitation under the intended attendee account and respond only when exactly one usable self attendee is present.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the invitation from the selected attendee account. Respond only when Google marks exactly one attendee as self; do not edit another attendee response.

How to verify the fix

  • Only the intended account's uniquely identified self response is changed.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
